what I ended up building lets the agents I already have hand the task to each other when one runs out. but I'm genuinely curious if there's a workflow I'm missing.

Title: Claude Usage Tracker: A floating widget to track Claude usage limits in real time. | Product Hunt
# Claude Usage Tracker. ## A floating widget to track Claude usage limits in real time. A floating desktop widget that shows your Claude.ai usage limits in real time. Launch tags:Productivity•User Experience•Artificial Intelligence. No reviews yetBe the first to leave a review for Claude Usage Tracker. Wispr Flow: Dictation That Works Everywhere. Wispr Flow: Dictation That Works Everywhere — Stop typing. I use Claude heavily for coding and writing, and I kept hitting the usage limit at the worst possible times — right in the middle of a task. The only way to check was to open Claude.ai, navigate to the settings, and manually look at the usage page. I was doing this constantly throughout the day. I wanted something that just sat on my screen and told me at a glance — like a battery indicator, but for Claude. So I built a small floating widget that shows my usage as a progress bar with a countdown timer. It lives in the system tray and never gets in my way. The Chrome extension handles authentication automatically, so there's no manual token copying or login. Everything stays on your machine — no servers, no accounts. If you're a heavy Claude user on Windows, I hope this saves you from the same frustration. Would love to hear feedback!

results.title: Moxie: Use any AI with Claude Code, switch accounts mid-task | Product Hunt
results.content:
Title: Moxie: Use any AI with Claude Code, switch accounts mid-task | Product Hunt
## Use any AI with Claude Code, switch accounts mid-task. Moxie is a Mac menu bar app for Claude Code. Use your ChatGPT plan, Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenRouter or local models in Ollama, all from the Claude Code you already use. Pick another account in one click and keep the same session going. Every account's 5-hour and weekly limits sit in the menu bar. I spend most of my day in Claude Code, and two things kept breaking my flow: hitting the 5-hour limit halfway through a task, and wanting to try other models without leaving the tool I already know. So I built Moxie, a small Mac app that lives in the menu bar: • Use any AI with Claude Code: your ChatGPT plan, Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, or local models in Ollama. One click, and the same session keeps going on your other account. • See every account's 5-hour and weekly limits, with a heads-up before you run out. • It sets up Claude Code for you, in the CLI and the VS Code extension. Everything runs on your Mac. Keys stay in your Keychain, requests go straight to the provider you pick, and there's no Moxie account. I'd love your feedback: which model would you run Claude Code on first, and what's missing for your setup? Better yet, switch a claude account with another Claude account and get the same model handling it. when you switch accounts mid-task does the actual conversation context/history carry over to the new account, or does Claude Code just start a fresh session and you're re-explaining where you left off? that also means the thing Chris raised above is the real tradeoff, not the handoff mechanics: if you swap from Claude to a different model mid-task, the new model inherits the conversation history but not the judgment calls the first model was quietly making. does Moxie default to keeping you on the same model family when one account is low, and only cross to a different model as a last resort, or is it indifferent to which model picks up the thread? @galdayan You control what model picks it up when you switch the account.

results.title: Peras: Pause Claude Code and Codex before they burn your week | Product Hunt
results.content:
I kept running out of Claude Code mid-week and got tired of constantly spamming /usage to guess how much a task would eat. So I built a guard. You pick a line, like 85% of the week, and when Claude Code or Codex crosses it, the next tool call is refused with a plain reason. You can resume whenever you want, for an hour or until the reset. It started as a SwiftBar menu. Later I rewrote the menu in native because it gave me more room to customise it. The CLI and hooks are free and MIT. The Mac app is €4.99 once, which is basically paying me to sign and ship it.You can also build it yourself from the repo. The catches: it's macOS only (Linux might work but isn't tested), it's for subscriptions, Codex hooks fail open if the hook itself breaks, and `claude -p` can't be stopped. Curious what % [...] and once usage crosses it, the agent's next tool call is refused with a plain reason, so one long task can't burn the rest of your week. Resume whenever you want, from the terminal or the menu bar. Opt-in: your agents can be told their own usage. The CLI and hooks are free and MIT. The native Mac menu bar app is €4.99 once.
